title: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Everything in this class is out of what was written aforetime, and it was written for us to learn.

We are all here because we believe. We are not here for a social event, and not because we just like seeing each other. We are here because we all fear the Most High, and understanding that, we have to fear him in everything. Everything, sisters, and that includes how a wife carries herself toward her husband.

A lot of our relationships are skewed. Before everybody it is shalom, Most High and Christ blessed, and it looks beautiful; but at home it is something else. A lot of sisters, no matter how long they have been in the truth, do not have a grasp of what their role and demeanor toward their husband is supposed to be. The men of the Lord understand how hard that fight is for them, because we understand the original sin and where it all began. They are the weaker vessel, Satan is lurking, and typically the woman is the door. That is why classes like this have to constantly remind them.

Go to the beginning, where it all started. “And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” This is the creation of man, the Lord forming him from the dust of the ground. The first man was a man of color.

“It is not good that the man should be alone”. Don't just look at the words on the page; envision it. The Lord created man and said it is not good for him to be by himself.

“I will make him an help meet for him.” An help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living. She was something to his liking. She was made for him.

The Lord “formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them”. God gave Adam the ability to name the creatures. Adam was not equal to them and not underneath them: he was over them. He was given power over them; the man was at the top. “And whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.”

“But for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Out of all the beasts of the field there was still nothing to Adam's liking, nothing that was just for him.

“And the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs”, and from that rib he made a woman “and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High God doing this for his son. That is a gift.

The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman that was made just for you, because it is not good that man should be alone.

“This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” She was taken from man. That is where she came from, and that is what she was made for: a help meet for her husband.

Out of all the beasts of the field nothing could make the man as happy as what God specialized in and made for him, a woman. That woman has a purpose. Sometimes the help starts to think that they are the purpose, that they are the house, not realizing: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept that, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself. It is only when you decide to leave that place that there is turmoil.

precepts.why:
The gift of Genesis 2 still remains for every man. “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity”. That takes application: to live joyfully is something you have to make happen. You have to do it.

“Which he hath given thee under the sun”: he, the Most High, has given her to you. This woman, this rib, was made for you, and God made her for you.

“For that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” That is the portion you have been given in this life, with all the work you do under the sun. God made you a rib; he gave you your portion, and your portion is her.

So there is no confusion as to why the woman was made: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? Shut up; you don't know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord. Argue with God.

“Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.” This is simple: God created the woman for the man. Nobody can create or remake their purpose in life.

Do you know how much happier you would be if you accepted your role and your purpose on this earth? That goes for the men, and it applies to our sisters. So many spend their lives fighting against gravity and God, fighting against their God-given purpose. You can't change it, and trying to change it only brings confusion. That is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not.

And you wonder why you are dealing with all these spirits, depression and anxiety, always on tens. It is because you are fighting against your God-given role.

sense.text:
Here is where it all went left. “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field”. He asked the woman, “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” and she answered that of the tree in the midst of the garden “God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.”

She knew the order. She knew the rule and what was said; there was no confusion. All she had to do was obey.

“Ye shall not surely die”. The serpent picked up on something. That is what Satan does: he searches deep within you and knows things inside you that you are not even cognizant of.

“Ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” Satan knows the punch words, the catchphrases that get you thinking and play with your ear: gods. What was within the woman? Jealousy and envy of the position Adam was in over her; sedition, fighting against the power over her; mutiny. She wanted his spot. She wanted Adam's power.

Brothers, if you think for a second that she is not trying to overthrow you, you're an idiot. Don't ask them; they are not going to say, yes, I want to rule over you. It is not in them to say it; it is their spirit within them. The same thing happens wherever order and structure are put in place: some brothers want to be the HNIC, they don't like being told what to do, and they have a problem with structure. We see it all the way from the beginning.

“And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise”: now she liked it. Satan started scratching the itch that was already there, and he was telling her what her desire was. “She took of the fruit thereof, and did eat”.

From that point death entered into the world. There is no mistake worse than the mistake that was made there, because death entered into the world because of it.

precepts.why:
“Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.” In Corinth the women were trying to lead the church. They were out of their place, and Paul had to correct them. It may have been happening in other places too, but he had to put it in a letter, so it was plainly a problem. Tell your woman shut up. Be quiet. Let them learn in subjection, which is submission. Let them learn from their own husbands; it is not for them to be teaching people.

“For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” Paul went all the way back to the beginning to deal with the situation of the woman being disorderly. That is why the beginning is relevant now.

“And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” Some might think that is random for him to say. It is not. He is telling you what happens when you allow the woman to lead and get out of her place and out of her role.

“Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” Y'all forgot? That is what happened. Eve allowed the serpent to deceive her, and it was because of what was already within her. All she had to do was play her role, play her position and stay in order, and we might not be where we are right now. Because of that first mistake, we all die.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. You are asleep. The first woman, created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife is not?

Because the woman can be deceived, you as the head have to constantly remind her of her place and role in the home. “Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled”. If you go a little while without mentioning it, she starts to think maybe it is okay that I do this or speak like that. It takes routine maintenance: I'm the head, I run this, the Lord put me in this place, I am your lord.

The daughters of Sarah understand this and know they fight this spirit daily; when you remind them, they don't have a problem with it. It is only the Jezebels that find it offensive. When your husband sees an issue, sis, it is an issue. You are his help meet.

This is for the brothers who like to be gone from the house, the truckers and the ones gone long distance for long periods, and then wonder why they come home to a different person. You have to be there constantly reinforcing your standard, your rule and what you want from your wife, as well as exhorting, building her up and being her support. If you don't, you will come home to a whole new negro. You have been missing in action; she wakes up every morning and it is just her and the kids, and she thinks she is the head of the house. Then the kids don't even know you.

A hedge is protection; it is there to guard. You have to keep Satan at bay. If you leave your post, brother, the possession will be spoiled.

Of the woman came the beginning of sin, but why? “For pride is the beginning of sin”. That is what pushed her over: pride. Don't ever think your wife has no pride. That pride is wanting to be over you, to make the decisions; it is what she battles every day, and it runs into sin.

“And he that hath it shall pour out abomination”: resentment, hatred, a grudge toward you. Every time you try to correct it, they bring that resentment to you. “And therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” Don't let that pride seep into your house.

Paul made more than one reference to what happened at the beginning: “as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty”. Satan is able to see the things that are within you, and that is what he attacks: not where you are strong, but where you are weak.

Subtle means pleasing to the senses in a mild or nuanced way. That is how Satan works on the sisters when they get a little bit of power: I decide what we eat around here, I put up the curtains, I picked this out. It feels good, and then you start overstepping your bounds, not knowing that was Satan right there that set you up with the damn curtains. That is how subtle it is. So, sisters, when you see yourself starting to overstep your divine place and purpose, say, that's Satan; you almost got me. Paul warned us.

A lot of sisters forget it is the house of the man. Joshua said, as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say with the agreement of my wife. He commanded his home. That is the natural place of a man. And some brothers remove themselves from it and want to be a mama's boy in their marriage, wanting her to be their mother instead of leading her. That emboldens her, and now you are her child, a boy husband.

“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust.” That is where temptation comes from: it is something already within you. If you have a problem with wanting to be the head honcho, to be over your husband, to be the shot caller in control of how things go in the home, Satan plays with that, and you look up and there is a complete role reversal in your home.

Most of us have been infected by the westernized mindset. Birthdays, baby showers, Father's Day and Mother's Day, Thanksgiving, the ring on the finger: we do them because we think we are supposed to. We have been corrupted by rules that God didn't make, and because they have been normalized we think that is how life is. The same goes for how a man deals with his wife. Fathers told their sons, don't pay attention to them hoes; get your money, get a good job, and the hoes are going to come; you are going to have multiple. One father left a condom on his dresser for his son to take, and when it came up missing said, I put that there for you. That was normalized too, and when you come into this truth you see your pops was wicked: he was telling you to go fornicate. There is a lot of residue, on the brothers' side and on the sisters' side, that we try to bring into this truth and have to let go of completely, or it will cloud your judgment and ruin your marriage.

sense.text:
“The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” This shows how the Lord deals. The woman messed up and brought it back to Adam, and Adam entertained it. Now the Lord is in front of both of them, and Adam blamed the woman. Is that not what brothers do now?

That is why we don't give you any room, brothers. When your house is out of order, we look at you. You are the one who has to keep things aligned and in check, and if you are not doing it, it will be evident.
“And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.”

“And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” This is a prophetic scripture concerning the coming of the Messiah.

“I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children”. Before this mistake, giving birth did not look like what it is now, nor everything surrounding it: the pre- and postpartum, the pain, the menstrual cycle, the mental anguish many sisters go through. It is going to be painful and an ordeal.

“And thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Many women read this and think it was only because of what happened that he rules over them. No: go back to Genesis 2, where the order was already set. Here God says, get your butt back in your place. There is no question of what the role and position of a wife is to be.

Your desire shall be to your husband: his wants, his aspirations; what he sees fit is what you will see fit. If you want anything, it is from your husband. And he shall rule over thee. There is no question where the woman belongs and where the man belongs.

“Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife”: Adam, you listened to what she had to say, and “hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee”. So “cursed is the ground for thy sake”, “till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.”
“And Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” He gave her a name. The divine order was set in the beginning, and that is the order Paul goes back to.

precepts.why:
Read it again in case you forgot that the order was there before the fall. “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” The Lord brought every beast and fowl to Adam, “and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.” He was placed over each and every one of those creatures; he named them and had dominion over them.

“But for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Adam still needed something just right for him. So the Lord made the woman from his rib, “and Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman”. Just as he had dominion over the other creatures, he had dominion over the woman. He named her. She was his possession.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.” One flesh means together.

So when Genesis 3:16 says “he shall rule over thee”, it is not something new that started with the sin. It was already the order from the beginning.

sense.text:
The beginning was read first to show where the order was set. Paul is not making anything up. He did not make a list and decide to put this person here and that person there; he went to the divine order set forth from the beginning, and he did it more than once.

“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” The order goes: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or position, they are the damn devil. That goes for the men too: the ones who want to be a mama's boy. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

precepts.why: Paul says it in other places too. “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of the church.

“And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead”. Christ is the head of the church, and the husband is head of the wife even as Christ is head of the church.

“The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.” If you are still stuck on the Trinity, go sit in the corner somewhere; you just don't get it.

“For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth: and he will shew him greater works than these”. How could the Father show the Son if the Son was the Father? How could the Most High show his son something if they were the same entity? It makes no sense. The Trinity doctrine is crushed right there.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given: the Father said, this is what you can do. The headship of the household falls under that same order, as 1 Corinthians 11 shows.

“That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him.” To honor the Son means you honor what he said. So if you don't honor the order God has given you, you are not honoring the Lord; it is impossible.

If there is anything in the scripture that you say you just can't do, you are the devil. In every way possible you have to do what God said; there can be no commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle in something, and we know the fight; but never be the one who says, no, I'm not going to do it.

“I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” Christ himself is in the divine order, and he himself submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did? We can't say we are in the truth if we don't.

sense.text:
“Let your women keep silence in the churches”. This scripture has been taken out, remixed, and given all kinds of excuses, especially by the church, and it has all been done because of that order. There are beta men out there whose job is to appease the woman. It doesn't matter how crazy it is: the woman is God, she is the greatest thing to hit the planet and we should worship her. But she came from a man. It makes no sense.

You are being conditioned. It is happening everywhere, in podcasts and TV shows: these beta men do everything in their power to make the women comfortable, and that is what makes them popular. The saying, it ain't tricking if you got it, came from a beta simp, and now some women think that is the standard of a man.

What is happening here is that the Israelite man is being reformed. Everything you were told a man is supposed to be is being demolished, along with all the bad things. A man who was a whoremonger comes into the truth and has to shake that spirit off by being around men who love their wives and take care of their families. In the same way he has to shake the weak things he learned in the world, the things men were taught to do to get a woman, which go away once he has her. Sisters, you never had a male friend in your life unless he was a homo, and even then he was just trying to steal your secrets. Men were taught to do certain things to get the woman, and once they had her it all went away. We are teaching men how to truly love their wives.

A man should be chased and valued. The man is the prize. Bowing before a woman and asking for her hand in case she might say yes is a westernized mindset, and we are getting rid of all of it, sisters. We are coming back to righteousness.

“Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.” What does this have to do with wives respecting a husband? This is where it starts.

In a household where the laws of God are taught, where the structure and the ethical principles God gave are put in place, and the children honor their father and mother, those children grow up to break generational curses; if they keep those commandments, the sons will honor their wives and the daughters will honor their husbands, because they were taught when they were little and it keeps going forward.

Honor thy father and thy mother is the first principle, the first line of structure, in showing respect. A child learns it as a kid: that is my mom, that is my dad, I have to honor and respect what they say. And when they grow older, that is what they will demand from their own children.

A woman won't treat you how she treats her father; she will treat you how her mother treated her father. It is not foolproof, because children make their own choices; but a child who came up in a wholesome household, where the father and mother both understood the laws of God, operated within their roles and demanded obedience to God from their children, is more likely to carry that legacy on.

“If a woman also vow a vow unto the Lord, and bind herself by a bond, being in her father’s house in her youth; and her father hear her vow”. This is a vow she is making to God, and her father overhears it. The father has a choice: he can hold his peace and let it stand, or he can slap that vow down: no, Lord, that vow is not going to stand.

“But if her father disallow her in the day that he heareth; not any of her vows, or of her bonds wherewith she hath bound her soul, shall stand: and the Lord shall forgive her, because her father disallowed her.” This is a vow a child makes to God, and the father has the power to say, Lord, pay no mind to that. The Lord forgives her because her father stepped in.

“And if she had at all an husband, when she vowed”, and her husband heard it, “then her vows shall stand”. “But if her husband disallowed her on the day that he heard it; then he shall make her vow which she vowed, and that which she uttered with her lips, wherewith she bound her soul, of none effect: and the Lord shall forgive her.”

A married, grown woman makes a vow to the Lord, and her husband can say, Lord, don't pay attention to that; that vow doesn't stand. A man can stand in front of your vow with the Lord. He has the same amount of power over her that her father had.

What you are seeing is a transference of power. The father has power to give his daughter to whom he wishes, and when he does, he gives up his rights and his power over her to that man. If the husband has that much power, should she not honor her husband as she would honor her father? Absolutely. It is the same distance of respect: what a mother should receive from her children, a man should receive from his wife, a man shows to Christ, and Christ shows to his Father. Only the world tells you that once you are grown you are on the same level.

precepts.why:
This is how much power a father had over his daughter. “And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” If a man seduces your daughter and she consents and they lie together, he has to take her as his wife and pay the dowry. That is the law of God. If he doesn't, that is fornication. He has no option.

“If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him”: the father has a choice. He can say, I don't care that y'all lay together, you can't have her; and she will carry that shame, but he can't have her. The father has that power.

We don't understand how much power the father has in the home. And nothing changes when that father is a husband: the same amount of power he has over his children is the same amount of power he has over his wife. So where the hell is there room for disrespect? There is none.

sense.text:
“If any man take a wife, and go in unto her, and hate her, and give occasions of speech against her, and bring up an evil name upon her, and say, I took this woman, and when I came to her, I found her not a maid”. Who is this accusation against? The father. It is his household. He brought his daughter and said, this is my daughter, she is a virgin, I have taken care of her and watched over her.

Marrying off your daughter is a heavy thing, because it is a transference of power. If a father marries his daughter to a crazy negro, he failed; he didn't vet him. He is her protector. In giving her to you he is trusting that you will now protect her and see to her clothes, her food and where she lays her head. If he turns those rights over, he had better make sure you are the one.

“Then shall the father of the damsel, and her mother, take and bring forth the tokens of the damsel’s virginity unto the elders of the city in the gate”. All of that happened when the transference was made: the marriage papers, the tokens of virginity showing she was a virgin, proclaimed before Israel with a feast.

“I gave my daughter unto this man to wife, and he hateth her”, and he says he found her not a maid, “and yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s virginity.” That is the proof; this man is making an evil accusation against the daughter. “And they shall spread the cloth before the elders of the city.”
“And the elders of that city shall take that man and chastise him”: they beat the brakes off of him. There were stripes back then.

precepts.why:
“Hast thou children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth. Hast thou daughters? have a care of their body, and shew not thyself cheerful toward them.” Why not show yourself cheerful toward them? You are not to be your children's friend; you are their parent, the head of the household over them, and you lose sleep watching over them.

A daughter learns order in the household from the beginning. Her father is the first form of respect she has, honoring her father and her mother. Show yourself cheerful toward her and you blur the lines, and once the lines are blurred, so is her perception of authority. Then when she is grown, how is she going to deal with her husband?

“Marry thy daughter, and so shalt thou have performed a weighty matter”: because the man you marry her to now has the power you had over your beloved daughter, the little girl you brought into the world and lost sleep over. If you are going to give that power to somebody, you had better be damn sure he will do right by her. That is the father's job: to make sure he is the one.

sense.text:
“If thou wouldest get a friend, prove him first, and be not hasty to credit him.” This is why it is so important, brothers and sisters, to prove that you have truly found the one that is for you. It takes extensive research; you have to dig and search it out. Sisters, this is the man you are going to place over you.

Many single sisters come into the truth without a father in the truth looking for their husband, and a lot of that has been placed in their hands. But the way things were done, it didn't matter who you were interested in; it was your father's decision. We have been westernized to the point that we think that is crazy. In every case you read in the scriptures the father was choosing: a man went to the father and said, I want to marry your daughter, and the father said, you have to work seven years for me. She couldn't say, I'm good, Dad.

“For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of thy trouble.” Some friend, “being turned to enmity”, “will discover thy reproach”; some is “a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of thy affliction”; in prosperity “he will be as thyself”, but “if thou be brought low, he will be against thee, and will hide himself from thy face.”

“Separate thyself from thine enemies, and take heed of thy friends.” If the Lord tells us to do this with friends, how much more should we do it with a spouse?

Sisters, do you know the amount of authority you give a man when you decide to be his wife? You are saying, whatever he says, I'm going to do. If you find out after that he wants you to hop on one leg when he comes home from work, then you had better build up your calf muscles, because that is your head and you decided to make him your head.

In a perfect world everyone would be up front about who they are, but it isn't like that. Sometimes things are withheld. But if you truly believe, you have the Lord on your side. The Lord knows if he is unreasonable; the Lord knows if he is a demon. The Lord will take care of his daughters, whether by changing him, by taking him through the wringer until he sees the error of his ways, or sometimes by taking somebody out. The Lord is a just God, and if you are evil, the Lord will deal with you.

Back to respect being taught in childhood. “Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am the Lord your God.” The Lord understands the importance of structure, and it has always been there. You are to fear your mother and father even into old age. Don't think that once you are twenty you no longer have to listen; that power is always there. And you wives, once you become someone's wife, you have to deal with your husband.

precepts.why:
“Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.” It was so important for them to honor their father and mother so that their days would be prolonged and it would go well for them in the land.

The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation. When there is dysfunction, anything not aligned with how God set it up, it affects the whole nation. Households affect other households: if your house is out of order and your children play with another family's children, they learn the same bad behaviors. If your wife's best friend is a gossiper running from home to home, it is only a matter of time before your wife is called a gossiper too; if you kick it with the murmurers, the same happens to you. You will infect the nation if your household is not in order. God is about order, and always has been.

sense.text: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married”. Miriam, a woman, was speaking with Aaron, and they were mad about what Moses had going on.

“Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.” What was Miriam doing? Murmuring. She wanted to lead. She was putting herself on the same level as Moses, making herself equal to the men and putting herself where she didn't belong. Some might say God was only upset that she said it. No; not when you read what happened.
“Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.”
“Miriam became leprous, white as snow”. Miriam had to learn the hard way: the Lord had to turn her into a white woman.

“If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days?” That does not mean we spit in our kids' faces. It means that if her father had taught her to respect authority, she would not be murmuring and trying to take control. She should have been humbled as a child. She should never have felt comfortable speaking the way she spoke; a woman is not supposed to feel comfortable being like that toward men in any capacity.

It goes back to what she learned as a child. Many of us are disrespected in our homes because of what our wives learned and saw growing up, and the same is true of how we men function. That is why it is of the utmost importance to apply the laws in our households today, so our children are not affected and can grow the way they are supposed to.

God took that disrespect toward leadership personally, and he intervened. Aaron spoke too, and nothing happened to him; it was the woman who got it, because she stepped out of her place.

“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.” As unto the Lord means the same respect you would show to Christ is the respect you should show to your husband.

There are going to be sisters who find out they will not get the kingdom because they did not respect nor reverence their husbands. Every command your husband gives you is law. It is like getting orders from God. As long as your husband is not asking you to sin, if he asks you to do something, it is sin if you don't do it.

The westernized mindset in our women says, he has that much power? You malfunction because you don't believe he is a god; you don't see the Christ in him; you don't think God would give a man on earth that much control over you. Read your Bible. He absolutely has that much control over you.

You can see a lot about a person by how they deal with their spouse. Your level of faith is shown by the level of respect you have for your husband, because that is the level of respect you have for God. And the way a man loves and takes care of his wife is the level of love and care he has for Christ. If you don't love, protect and provide for her, you are an infidel. If you don't respect your husband and do what he says, you are an infidel, fringes or no fringes, every Sabbath day or not.

If a woman won't submit to you, she has already decided you are weak and not worthy of leading her, and the red flags usually show in the beginning, but lust makes a man look past them.

precepts.why:
“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?” They will have the audacity: Lord, I taught classes, I was out in the streets handing out flyers, I didn't eat pork, I left the shrimp alone, I wore fringes every day.

“And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” What keeps them from being known of the Lord? Iniquity, sin. And a wife not submitting to her husband is sin. Yes, a disrespectful wife can miss the kingdom; did you not realize that?

This makes complete sense to the brothers' side of the room. “But if any provide not for his own”: her food, her raiment, her clothing. If a man doesn't take care of his wife, “and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith”.

Lord, I didn't eat pork, I didn't eat shrimp, I didn't have no lobster, I stopped dealing with the prostitutes, I kept the Sabbath. But you didn't take care of your wife or your children; you were a deadbeat; you left the house and lived among everybody else doing what you wanted. That man hath denied the faith, “and is worse than an infidel.” Is that man going to see the kingdom? No.

So what makes anyone think it is different when a wife doesn't submit or respect her husband? It is the same: she is not in the truth, and she will not receive the kingdom.

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church”. Is that an option? Does a husband have to love his wife? If he doesn't, will he see the kingdom? No. And right beside it: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.” Neither one is an option.

The natural instinct of the evil man in this world is to leave: to go from woman to woman, to roam and be promiscuous with nothing holding him down, or to be in a relationship and still satisfy every lust he has. That is not love, and he will not see the kingdom.

sense.text:
“Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Why does Paul keep repeating it? Because this is evidence of your faith. Paul called marriage a mystery. Here is a hint: the leaders' leadership began with their household. Being able to deal with people, to have compassion and care and true love for the body, began with their wives; and the same goes the other way.

There is no room for options there. Nowhere in the scripture does it say you can respect him as long as he does this or that. If that is in your mind, know that you are led by the damn devil. Nobody says, I won't eat pork unless; or I'll keep the Sabbath if.

Reverence is deep respect for someone or something; that is what Paul told you to have for your husband.

precepts.why:
Your whole duty in life, your whole purpose: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments”. There is no excuse for not observing a commandment.

If you are being beaten in a relationship, we are not telling you to stay, sis. If he is beating you to a pulp and injuring you, get away from him; don't die. He obviously isn't keeping the commandments if he is harming you. But if he is not asking you to sin, you have no reason. You can't say, I'll respect him as long as he does this. You show him by your chaste conversation and your actions that you are going to serve the Lord no matter what, and you heap hot coals on his head. Disrespect should never be an option; only Satan gives you that option.

If submission to your husband depends on his behavior, it is not submission; it is manipulation. God told wives to submit to their husbands in everything, with no caveat: I'll submit if he acts right, if he doesn't offend me. Submission is not a transaction; it is a spiritual assignment from God.

sense.text:
“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.” Paul addresses this in almost all his writings. As it is fit in the Lord means as the Lord designed it. Can you truly say you are in the truth and not respect that man? You can't, no matter how long you have been sitting here.

Brothers, we know what it is like coming from the world. Just as we have residue we are trying to beat, our wives do too. They are the weaker vessel, and many times they are the doorway to Satan himself; that is typically how Satan comes in to destroy the house. Knowing that, we have to dwell with them according to knowledge and cast down every imagination contrary to the word of God, and the only way to do that is with the scriptures. Just as we have to be reminded, they have to be reminded.

Sisters, your toughest plight in this truth is going to be honoring your husband, your lord. That is the everyday battle. Just as you listen to the boss on the job, your husband is supposed to get umpteen times more respect than him, and you don't clock out. Everything about a woman, even her anatomy, tells her she is to be submissive. It is unnatural for a woman to go from her father's house to being independent and then find a husband; you were never designed to be alone. You were always to be under leadership.

Respect is a feeling of deep admiration: esteem, regard, admiration, veneration, awe, reverence. That is what you are supposed to have for your husband, even if he snores, has a bad back or limps when he walks. Don't change the definition of respect or reverence to fit you. Do it and you will have more peace, because it is the natural order of how you were made.

We have normalized dysfunction to the point that we think arguing is just troubles of the flesh. Imagine arguing with Christ; you can't even put it together in your mind. If Christ said, park right here, the car would be parked right there every day. Go back and forth with the boss at work every day and he will tell you, get your ass out of here, I'm the boss, you do what I say. Sisters, it is your role to do what your husband says, every day, all the time, every time.

A righteous man will do anything to see his wife happy; no sane man wants to come home to his wife in anguish. A daughter who comes running to the door, Daddy!, gets whatever she wants. When the demeanor changes, the answer becomes no. Sisters, if you want, you have to be a princess. Reverence him, give him that respect, make him feel like everything he is supposed to be, a god on earth, and watch what happens. That takes a mind that is reborn: not using what you have to get what you want, but having your spirit right. Women of the world were taught to use what they have to get what they want, all physical, while the spirit inside was no good; but a righteous man needs your spirit to be right. Get your spirit right and you will see the Ephesians 5 man you want. Leslie Jones says marriage is legal slavery, because she has a spirit that is not right in her: it is confrontation with every man, and they leave her.

We know what was done to us historically: the home was split up, Esau stepped in and replaced the man in the home, and the men allowed it; the crack epidemic took many men out of the home, the women had to fend for themselves, and disdain for the men grew. We are the only nation whose women say, we don't need a man, and then depend on the system. But we are not that same man now; we are taking back what belongs to us. Not every man deserves respect, and some brothers have done things that would make anyone understand why she is like that. But, sis, if you love the Lord, you had better respect him anyway. Your respect has nothing to do with him; it is a reflection of your belief and faith in Christ. Without it you are just as bad as him; you are an infidel too.

“That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands”. Why do the young women need to be taught to love their husbands? Because it is not in them unless you teach them. That is why the older women need to teach their young daughters how to love their husbands. It is a never-ending cycle.

Do you understand what happens to a man when he feels disrespected? Society has blinded all our minds, and you don't realize the realm you are stepping into. That is why there is domestic violence and broken families among us. Yet even men: if you are not answering disrespect with the scriptures, with the Bible, brother, you are not in the truth either. Somebody has to be spiritual in the situation.

The moment a woman stops respecting her man, his attraction to her dies. A man builds a house the right way, lays the foundation, gets the plumbing right, brings his family in, and nothing will harm that house worse than a disrespectful woman. Adultery will ruin a household; but the word no to a man who is head of the house is a deal breaker. If he does not have full subjection over you, he can't protect you; you are now under some other man, and you are not his.

At the same time, brothers, sisters speak out of emotion; so do you. She might say no, but watch what she does, then respond.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives”. This is for a wife married to a man who is pleased to dwell with her though he does not obey the word. Through her chaste conversation she can win that man over.

It is through her example: look what the word of God has done for me, and how I deal with you now. He thinks, she used to be loud and obnoxious and argue with me; now when I ask her to do something she does it; she doesn't question my authority or challenge me. The word did that? Let me go see what those brothers in purple and gold are talking about. Through your submission you can move mountains with a man.

When a husband is wrong and his wife, who was right, still says, okay, I'll do it, I'm sorry, and goes on with her day, it changes him. He is left with hot coals on his head, knowing she is more righteous than he is, because she stood down out of respect for him as the man with the final say.

Disrespect switches a man off: he no longer sees her intellect or her beauty. Go far enough and there is a point of no return, where everything she does looks like disrespect to him because he is used to it. Coming back from that takes major submissive work. Be so far from disrespect that he thinks you were sent from God.

The signs that she doesn't respect the Christ in you: she talks over you and won't let you lead the conversation; once he has come to his conclusion, sis, stand down, and give your input later. She corrects or embarrasses you publicly, when a respectful woman covers her man and makes him look good. She ignores your instructions or treats your leadership like a suggestion; whatever your husband says to get done, you should be racing to get it done like you race the sun before the Sabbath, and it does not have to make sense to you. She speaks with attitude or contempt; speak to your husband the way you want your children to speak to you. She doesn't value your presence; be eager when he walks through the door and adjust to what he likes. She competes with you instead of supporting you; your wife is not supposed to be your opposition, so hold your tongue and make his decision the best it can be. She shares your business with others; if he wants them to know, let him tell them. She doesn't seek your counsel and makes decisions without you. She disrespects you in subtle ways: eye rolls, sighs, dismissive looks. She won't be quiet when you talk, though she is quiet when her boss talks.

“Hast thou a wife after thy mind? forsake her not”. Very few understand that this is not their show. It is about the house of the man. A wife after your mind is a woman who understands that she is in subjection to you, that you are the head of the home, and that what you want is what she wants. She makes your desires her desires, your aspirations her aspirations; how you want things to be is how she wants them to be, because she understands her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself. If her husband wants the household a certain way, she makes it that way. That is her job as the manager of the house: to make sure the CEO is happy. The world told you, no, it's yours, sis, do what you want to do.

The last sign she does not respect the Christ in you is that she doesn't follow your lead spiritually and picks and chooses what to follow in this truth. And a bonus sign: she disrespects other men. If other men complain about your wife's demeanor, you are in denial; she has normalized disrespecting you, so she has no problem disrespecting other men. A woman's demeanor is supposed to change when she speaks to a man. She openly disagrees with leadership and order, when if her father had but spit in her face she would know it is not her place to speak on what leadership has said. She steps out of her role when she thinks she is right, and pride has her on tens. There is never a time when it is permissible for a woman to step out of the place of a woman.

The female's role is to support the male. The man's job is to build; the woman's job is to nest and to teach values to their offspring, and she needs a husband for that first.

“For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Nothing should be able to separate you from the love of God.

Sisters, the love of God causes you to respect your husband. Respect your king. Nothing, not even him, can you allow to take you away from that.
